section.name: Relationship to AMBI, ALTA, DORMS and MC_INTEGRITY
section.t: This appendix is informative. It places this document beside the work it descends from, in terms of what each document says; it makes no claim about what those documents' authors intend.

AMBI (). The digest of is the AMBI pseudoheader of its Section 3.4.2, with the same field layout, and the hold queue and consume-on-admission rule of are those of its Section 3.2. Two things differ. AMBI's Sections 3.4.2.1, 3.4.2.2, 3.4.2.6 and 3.4.2.7 take the addresses and ports from the packet on the wire; this document takes them from the flow's metadata, so that one digest verifies on whatever carrier delivers the datagram. AMBI's Section 3.3 manifest carries a stream identifier, a manifest sequence number, a first packet sequence number, an extensible TLV space (its Section 3.3.1.6) and digests, but no signature, and relies on its transport (Section 4.1: any authenticating transport; Sections 4.2 to 4.4: HTTPS, TLS and DTLS, all unicast) for authenticity; its Section 2.1.1 admits a protocol that signs manifests and delivers them over a multicast transport as a manifest delivery to be defined elsewhere, and this document's record is that delivery, defined as a separate signed record rather than an AMBI TLV so that it is a fixed layout, verified before any parsing and carried on the flow's own (S, G). AMBI's Sections 3.3.1.2 and 4.4 provide loss tolerance by overlapping successive manifests; this document uses non-overlapping windows and a byte-identical twin instead, so that a window's digests are inserted once and the replay floor and consume-once rule interact with nothing. AMBI names its hash algorithm in its YANG model; this document carries a Named Information Suite ID in the signed record.

ALTA (Asymmetric Loss-Tolerant Authentication, ). AMBI's Section 4.1 reserves a place for ALTA, which authenticates a multicast stream with an acyclic graph of message authentication codes (MACs) and regularly paced digital signatures. This document instead signs each window once and relies on the twin for loss: one signature per 37 datagrams, no MAC chain and no dependency between windows.

DORMS (). DORMS discovers a RESTCONF server for an (S, G) through reverse DNS (its Section 2.2) and serves YANG-modelled metadata from it, with a per-origin CORS grant that its Section 2.3.5 recommends and its Section 4.5 relies on against unauthorized pages. The well-known document of carries the same kind of metadata and the same grant from the source address itself under a certificate for that address, with no DNS hop, and treats a wildcard grant as no grant. DORMS's Section 2.2 lets a client with another way of finding a trusted server skip the DNS step, so a DORMS record remains one way to deliver the parameters of .

MC_INTEGRITY (). The multicast extension for QUIC carries packet hashes in MC_INTEGRITY frames sent from server to client (its Section 10.5), either on the client's unicast QUIC connection or on a multicast channel whose packets an earlier frame verified, a Merkle tree whose root the unicast connection carries (its Section 4.5), each a hash of the encrypted channel packet (its Section 7.1), and names its hash algorithm from the same Named Information Hash Algorithm Registry this document uses. A receiver with no per-receiver QUIC connection, one behind an AMT relay, in a broadcast or in a browser without one, cannot anchor that tree, which is the case this document serves; the two carry different digests over different bytes and cannot share them, so they complement each other by deployment, not by format.

section.name: Acknowledgments
section.t: The digest pseudoheader, the hold queue and the consume-on-admission rule of this document are those of AMBI, and the per-origin grant of the well-known document descends from DORMS; the threat model this document answers is that of the MBONED multicast security draft. The author thanks the authors of those documents, Jake Holland, Kyle Rose and Max Franke, for the work this builds on. No endorsement of this document by them is implied.
